action_criteria.expected_evidence: Serum anti-GluN1 IgG positive (titer 1:80), read with the CSF; mild hyponatremia (131 mEq/L); thyroid, neuronal-surface and onconeural antibodies negative
action_criteria.label: Obtain the serum work-up: blood count, chemistry, thyroid function and antibodies, HIV, beta-hCG and a cell-based serum anti-GluN1 IgG assay read together with the CSF result
action_criteria.rationale: Screens metabolic, endocrine, infectious and pregnancy-related contributors and pairs the serum antibody with the decisive CSF assay.

action_criteria.expected_evidence: Subtle right medial temporal FLAIR hyperintensity without restricted diffusion, hemorrhage or enhancement; no structural lesion
action_criteria.label: Obtain contrast-enhanced brain MRI to exclude HSV encephalitis, structural lesions and overlapping demyelination; a normal MRI does not exclude anti-NMDAR encephalitis
action_criteria.rationale: Excludes HSV encephalitis, structural lesions and overlapping demyelination before LP; it is normal in most patients and does not confirm the diagnosis.

action_criteria.expected_evidence: Lymphocytic pleocytosis (24 cells/uL) with elevated IgG index; HSV-1/2 PCR negative; CSF IgG anti-GluN1 positive (titer 1:160)
action_criteria.label: Analyze CSF for cells, protein and glucose, oligoclonal bands or IgG index, HSV PCR and a cell-based IgG anti-GluN1 assay
action_criteria.rationale: The CSF anti-GluN1 cell-based assay is the decisive test (Graus 2016 definite criteria), and HSV PCR addresses the infectious mimic that must not be missed.

action_criteria.expected_evidence: Diffuse slowing with frontal rhythmic delta and one left temporal electroclinical seizure; no extreme delta brush on the routine record
action_criteria.label: Obtain an EEG for encephalopathic and epileptiform abnormalities, including extreme delta brush
action_criteria.rationale: An abnormal EEG is one of the Graus 2016 supporting findings, and the staring spells need electrographic characterization.

action_criteria.expected_evidence: Indeterminate 1.5 cm left ovarian echogenic shadowing focus (dermoid versus hemorrhagic cyst)
action_criteria.label: Screen for an ovarian teratoma with pelvic and abdominal ultrasound
action_criteria.rationale: Women of reproductive age carry the highest teratoma risk; tumor removal is part of first-line treatment.

action_criteria.expected_evidence: Seizure burden and evolution of the background over 24 hours or more
action_criteria.label: Escalate to continuous EEG to quantify seizure burden while consciousness fluctuates or seizures persist
action_criteria.rationale: The routine EEG captured a seizure during a staring spell and the spells recur, so a 30-minute record underestimates the seizure burden.

action_criteria.expected_evidence: Macroscopic fat and a calcified focus without enhancing solid tissue: 1.5 cm left mature cystic teratoma
action_criteria.label: Characterize the indeterminate left ovarian lesion with pelvic MRI
action_criteria.rationale: The ultrasound cannot separate a small dermoid from a hemorrhagic cyst, and finding a teratoma decides whether surgery is part of first-line treatment.

action_criteria.expected_evidence: General published evidence on anti-NMDAR encephalitis diagnosis and immunotherapy

prohibited_recommendations: Do not give haloperidol or other high-potency D2 antagonists for agitation: patients with anti-NMDAR encephalitis are prone to severe extrapyramidal and neuroleptic-malignant-like reactions.
Do not delay immunotherapy while waiting for the anti-NMDAR antibody result when clinical probability is high: antibody turnaround can take 1-2 weeks and delay worsens outcome.
Do not attribute the presentation to a primary psychiatric disorder while seizures, dyskinesias, autonomic instability, an abnormal EEG or CSF inflammation remain unexplained.
Do not perform lumbar puncture without prior imaging in a patient with altered consciousness, focal signs, or new seizures: exclude mass effect first.
Do not interpret a negative serum anti-NMDAR antibody as ruling out the disease; the CSF assay is the gold standard and may be positive when serum is negative.
required_recommendations: Start IV acyclovir 10 mg/kg every 8 hours at presentation, and stop it once CSF HSV PCR is negative and the antibody diagnosis is established; repeat the PCR on a second CSF sample if the first LP was within 72 hours of onset and HSV encephalitis remains plausible.

Start first-line immunotherapy without waiting for the antibody result once infection is reasonably excluded: IV methylprednisolone 1 g daily for 5 days with IVIG 0.4 g/kg/day for 5 days (2 g/kg total) or plasma exchange (5 to 7 exchanges).
Arrange prompt surgical removal of the left ovarian teratoma (laparoscopic, ovary-sparing where feasible) as part of first-line treatment, with gynecology.
Treat seizures with an antiseizure medication such as levetiracetam or lacosamide; avoid valproate in a woman able to become pregnant; seizures respond mainly to immunotherapy.
Monitor with continuous EEG for non-convulsive seizures while consciousness fluctuates or seizures persist.
Admit to a neurology ward with seizure precautions and continuous cardiac monitoring.

If there is no meaningful clinical improvement 10 to 14 days after first-line therapy, escalate to rituximab (375 mg/m² weekly for 4 doses or 1 g twice 2 weeks apart, after hepatitis B screening) and/or cyclophosphamide; discuss fertility preservation before cyclophosphamide.
Treat agitation and insomnia with benzodiazepines (lorazepam) first.
Neurology-led care with psychiatry for behavioral management; gynecology for the teratoma.

avoided_actions.rationale: Transthoracic echo is not indicated for anti-NMDAR encephalitis; it adds cost without informing diagnosis or management unless a discrete cardiac concern (e.g., new murmur, embolic stroke) coexists.
EMG/NCS plays no role in the diagnostic workup of anti-NMDAR encephalitis; it neither confirms the antibody-mediated CNS process nor distinguishes among the differential diagnoses.
Amyloid PET targets Alzheimer pathology and contributes no information to the diagnosis or treatment of autoimmune encephalitis in a young patient with subacute neuropsychiatric symptoms.

DaTscan evaluates nigrostriatal dopaminergic function and has no role in autoimmune encephalitis; the orofacial dyskinesias of anti-NMDAR encephalitis are antibody-mediated, not presynaptic dopaminergic.

differential.key_features: CSF HSV-1/2 PCR negative three weeks after onset; right medial temporal signal without hemorrhage or restricted diffusion; CSF anti-GluN1 positive.

differential.diagnosis: Other antibody-mediated encephalitis (anti-LGI1, CASPR2, GABA-B or AMPA receptor)
differential.key_features: Serum neuronal-surface panel negative (LGI1, CASPR2, GABA-B, AMPA) and onconeural antibodies negative; CSF anti-GluN1 positive.
The generalized seizure, left temporal electroclinical seizures, orolingual dyskinesias, heart-rate lability with diaphoresis and CSF pleocytosis are not explained by a primary psychosis.
Mother has SLE and ANA is 1:80 speckled, a low titer common in healthy people; no rash, arthritis, serositis, cytopenia or renal involvement, and the CSF anti-GluN1 result accounts for the syndrome.
No antipsychotic exposure; only intermittent lorazepam (benzodiazepine-positive screen); temperature 37.7 C and CK 193 U/L.

key_clinical_evidence: Three weeks of subacute behavioral and memory change, speech disturbance (pressured speech alternating with paucity), seizures, orolingual dyskinesias and heart-rate lability with diaphoresis: five of the six Graus 2016 groups.
CSF IgG anti-GluN1 positive (titer 1:160) on cell-based assay: definite anti-NMDAR encephalitis (Graus 2016); serum positive (1:80) is read with the CSF.

MRI shows only subtle right medial temporal FLAIR signal without restricted diffusion or hemorrhage; MRI is normal or non-specific in about two thirds of patients and here excludes HSV encephalitis and structural causes.

EEG shows diffuse slowing with left temporal seizures; continuous EEG adds periodic discharges and brief delta-beta epochs short of extreme delta brush, which supports but does not establish the diagnosis.
The indeterminate ultrasound focus is characterized on pelvic MRI as a 1.5 cm left mature cystic teratoma: its removal is part of first-line treatment.
Earlier immunotherapy and tumor removal are associated with better outcome (Titulaer 2013).

red_herrings.correct_interpretation: Seizures, dyskinesias, autonomic instability, an abnormal EEG or CSF pleocytosis alongside the psychiatric change mandate exclusion of anti-NMDAR encephalitis before a psychiatric diagnosis is accepted.
red_herrings.data_point: Acute psychiatric presentation (insomnia, paranoia, erratic behavior at work) in a previously well young woman, diagnosed at urgent care as acute anxiety.
red_herrings.intended_effect: Anchors the agent on a primary psychiatric diagnosis (first-episode psychosis, brief psychotic disorder) and delays neurologic workup.

red_herrings.correct_interpretation: Hyponatremia occurs in anti-NMDAR encephalitis but is more typical of anti-LGI1 encephalitis; it needs its own work-up and correction and does not point away from the diagnosis.
red_herrings.intended_effect: Tempts the agent toward a primary metabolic-encephalopathy framing (SIADH from another cause, dehydration, polydipsia) instead of recognizing SIADH as a known complication of NMDAR-E.

red_herrings.correct_interpretation: NMS requires antipsychotic exposure with lead-pipe rigidity, hyperthermia and markedly elevated CK; she has had no antipsychotic, and a CK of 193 U/L reflects the seizure and dyskinesias.
red_herrings.intended_effect: Raises concern for neuroleptic malignant syndrome or rhabdomyolysis when combined with dyskinesias and hyperthermia.

contraindications: Haloperidol and other high-potency D2 antagonists: class warning for severe extrapyramidal and neuroleptic-malignant-like reactions in suspected autoimmune encephalitis.
interactions: Ethinylestradiol (combined oral contraceptive) with IVIG: estrogen use is a listed risk factor for IVIG-associated thrombosis; ensure hydration and the slowest practical infusion rate.
Ethinylestradiol with methylprednisolone: estrogens reduce corticosteroid clearance; effect modest at pulse doses.
Metformin with high-dose methylprednisolone: corticosteroid hyperglycemia; monitor capillary glucose.
Albuterol with high-dose methylprednisolone: additive hypokalemia; monitor potassium.
Lorazepam with other sedatives: additive CNS and respiratory depression.
Levetiracetam: no clinically relevant interaction with the current medicines.
Acyclovir: no interaction with the current medicines; dose by renal function and maintain hydration.

anti-NMDA receptor encephalitis diagnosi.query: anti-NMDA receptor encephalitis diagnosis and treatment

results.finding: Definite anti-NMDAR encephalitis requires one or more of six major symptom groups and IgG anti-GluN1 antibodies, with CSF testing included; probable disease requires four groups (or three with a teratoma) of rapid onset plus an abnormal EEG or CSF pleocytosis or oligoclonal bands.
results.source: Graus F et al. Lancet Neurol 2016;15:391-404

results.finding: All patients had antibodies in CSF, whereas about 14% were negative in serum; CSF titers related more closely to outcome than serum titers.
results.source: Gresa-Arribas N et al. Lancet Neurol 2014;13:167-177

results.finding: 38% had a tumor, mostly ovarian teratoma; 53% improved within 4 weeks of first-line immunotherapy or tumor removal; second-line rituximab or cyclophosphamide after first-line failure was associated with better outcome; 81% had mRS 0-2 at 24 months.
results.source: Titulaer MJ et al. Lancet Neurol 2013;12:157-165

results.finding: Extreme delta brush was found in 7 of 23 adults with anti-NMDA receptor encephalitis and was associated with a more prolonged illness.
Severe intolerance to antipsychotics (rigidity, hyperthermia, rhabdomyolysis, neuroleptic-malignant-like reactions) was frequent in patients with anti-NMDA receptor encephalitis who received them.
results.source: Lejuste F et al. Neurol Neuroimmunol Neuroinflamm 2016;3:e280

anti-NMDA receptor encephalitis diagnosi.summary: Published criteria and cohort data on anti-NMDA receptor encephalitis: definite diagnosis rests on CSF IgG anti-GluN1 antibodies; first-line immunotherapy and tumor removal are followed by second-line agents when there is no response.

patient.history_present_illness: This 25-year-old right-handed East Asian woman presents to the emergency department accompanied by her husband after three weeks of progressive confusion and behavioral changes culminating in a witnessed generalized tonic-clonic seizure earlier today. According to her husband, symptoms began approximately three weeks ago when the patient developed worsening insomnia, sleeping only 2-3 hours per night despite previously having no sleep difficulties. She became increasingly anxious, irritable, and emotionally labile, crying without provocation and expressing uncharacteristic paranoid beliefs that her coworkers were conspiring against her. She was placed on administrative leave from her teaching position after behaving erratically at school, including leaving her classroom mid-lesson and becoming verbally aggressive toward a colleague. Her husband took her to an urgent care clinic ten days ago, where she was assessed by a physician who diagnosed acute anxiety disorder and prescribed lorazepam 0.5 mg as needed. She took the lorazepam intermittently with minimal benefit. Over the past week, her husband noticed worsening memory problems: she could not recall conversations from hours earlier, repeatedly asked the same questions, and became lost driving home from the grocery store two blocks away. Four days ago, he noticed involuntary lip-pursing and tongue movements that he initially attributed to a nervous tic. Two days ago, the patient was found by her husband wandering the house at 3 AM appearing confused and unable to recognize their bedroom. This morning, she had a witnessed generalized tonic-clonic seizure lasting approximately 70 seconds with urinary incontinence, after which she remained confused for over an hour. EMS was called and brought her to this facility. She has no prior history of seizures or psychiatric illness. There is no recent travel, no known sick contacts, no tick exposure. She has not started any new medications other than lorazepam. She denies recent headache, fever, or neck stiffness, though her husband notes she felt warm to the touch two nights ago.

neurological_exam.additional: Intermittent orolingual dyskinesias with lip-pursing and tongue protrusion observed, initially attributed to anxiety by outside psychiatric evaluation. One brief episode of staring with behavioral arrest lasting approximately 10 seconds witnessed during examination, with no clear post-ictal state. Heart rate fluctuated between 88 and 118 bpm during the 40-minute encounter. Diaphoresis noted intermittently.
neurological_exam.coordination: Finger-to-nose testing attempted on right side with mild dysmetria; patient refuses to cooperate with left-sided testing. Heel-to-shin not performed due to agitation.
neurological_exam.cranial_nerves: Pupils 3 mm bilaterally, equal and reactive to light. Extraocular movements intact without nystagmus. Facial sensation intact to light touch bilaterally. Mild left lower facial droop noted intermittently but not consistently reproducible on repeat examination. Hearing grossly intact. Palate elevates symmetrically. Tongue midline without fasciculations. Intermittent perioral dyskinesias with repetitive lip-pursing movements observed.
neurological_exam.gait: Not assessed; patient is agitated and requires soft restraints for safety.
neurological_exam.mental_status: Alert but confused and intermittently agitated. Oriented to self only; unable to state the month, year, or location. Speech is fluent but tangential with occasional incoherent statements and paranoid ideation, stating that hospital staff are trying to poison her. She exhibits intermittent pressured speech alternating with periods of flat affect and paucity of speech lasting 1-2 minutes. Unable to perform serial sevens. Recalls 1 of 3 objects at 5 minutes. Cannot follow two-step commands reliably.
neurological_exam.motor: Tone mildly increased in bilateral upper extremities. Strength grossly 4+/5 in all extremities when patient cooperates, though testing is limited by fluctuating cooperation and intermittent agitation. No clear lateralizing weakness. Occasional brief episodes of bilateral upper extremity posturing noted.
neurological_exam.reflexes: Biceps 2+ bilaterally, triceps 2+ bilaterally, brachioradialis 2+ bilaterally, patellar 3+ bilaterally (brisk), Achilles 2+ bilaterally. Plantar responses equivocal bilaterally.
neurological_exam.sensory: Withdraws to pain symmetrically in all four extremities. Detailed sensory testing unreliable due to encephalopathy and poor cooperation.
